## What it is

- The **mbira** is the instrument of the **Shona** people of Zimbabwe; the mbira dzavadzimu ("voice of the ancestors") is played at ceremonies (bira) and social gatherings and is held sacred (Wikipedia, "Mbira").
- **22-28 keys** on a hardwood board (gwariva) in **three registers**: two on the left, one on the right; **bottle caps or shells** (machachara) buzz; it is often played inside a **deze**, a calabash resonator (Wikipedia). In 2020 the craft of making and playing mbira/sansi in Malawi and Zimbabwe went on UNESCO's list (Wikipedia).
- These are living traditions with their own teachers, names and ways of playing. The site's sound is a sketch from a few physics ideas, not the instrument; anything not from a source named on this page is marked unverified.

## How it sounds

- **Tunings** differ from family to family and do not sit on the piano's grid; **Nyamaropa** is close to Mixolydian, Katsanzaira to Dorian, Mavembe to Phrygian (Wikipedia). The site plays equal-tempered versions (unverified as mbira tunings).
- The **buzzers** rattle only while the board swings hard (a contact noise), so the buzz follows each pluck; the **deze** adds a low resonance and a longer ring (the site's amounts).
- Mbira music is often two interlocking parts, kushaura and kutsinhira (Wikipedia).

## Works Cited

<!-- works-cited: written by scripts/works-cited.py -->
::: {.works-cited}
"Lamellophone." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamellophone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamellophone). Plucked tines; many African names (mbira, likembe, kalimba, sanza); marimbula.

"Mbira." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mbira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mbira). Shona instrument of Zimbabwe; lamellophone; Hugh Tracey's kalimba (late 1950s) after the nyunga nyunga; inharmonic overtones strongest in the attack; adjacent tines vibrate; lowest notes in the centre is common; tunings not on the Western grid; Nyamaropa ~Mixolydian, Katsanzaira ~Dorian, Mavembe ~Phrygian; mbira dzavadzimu 22-28 keys, three registers (two left, one right); bottle-cap buzzers (machachara); deze calabash resonator; Nhema Musasa; UNESCO 2020.

**For students**

"Dumisani Maraire." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dumisani_Maraire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dumisani_Maraire). Nyunga nyunga mbira player; 1-15 number notation; Chemutengure.

"Stella Chiweshe." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stella_Chiweshe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stella_Chiweshe). Known internationally for mbira dzavadzimu; learned 1966-69 against taboos and colonial bans.
:::
